messages:
Priya Raman: FYI — following the outage earlier today, engineering posted a full RCA. Need a short customer-facing follow-up for impacted accounts. Can someone draft and I’ll review?

Alice Chen: I can paste a concise timeline + impact summary. Do we want to include the mitigation steps we performed live?

Miguel Torres: yes please include mitigation and planned preventive actions. Also clarify that no customer data was exposed.

Samir Patel: quick note from eng: root cause was a latent bug in the autoscaling delay path; under a burst of requests the replica bootstrap occasionally got stuck waiting for an internal lock. We rolled a hotfix that removes the lock for bootstrap and pushed a patch at 14:42 UTC.

Priya Raman: OK — I’ll assemble. Draft below — feedback welcome.

Priya Raman: DRAFT EMAIL:
Hi <customer>,

We’re writing to follow up on the service disruption that affected Redwood Inference hosted API between ~14:06–14:44 UTC today. We know interruptions like this are disruptive — we’re sorry and wanted to share what happened, what we did to restore service, and what we’re changing to prevent recurrence.

Summary of impact:
• A subset of requests to text-generation endpoints experienced errors and increased latencies, affecting ~3% of requests from active tenants.
• Customers that were actively sending long-sequence requests during the burst saw retries fail until the mitigation.
• No customer data was exfiltrated or modified as a result of this incident.

What we did during the incident:
• 14:06 UTC — anomalous error rate detected by alerts; incident on-call paged.
• 14:10 UTC — on-call (Alice) started live mitigation; we disabled the problematic autoscale policy and scaled an extra pool to drain queued requests.
• 14:24 UTC — first mitigation reduced error rate but elevated latency persisted for some requests.
• 14:42 UTC — engineering deployed a targeted patch that removed the bootstrap lock; request success rate returned to normal.
• 14:44 UTC — monitoring confirmed error rate and latency normalized; we closed the page.

Root cause (short):
• A rare lock contention during replica bootstrap under high burst workload caused a fraction of replicas to stall, leading to request failures and retries that amplified load.

Actions we’re taking (preventative):
• Immediate: hard rollouts of the patch across all regions (complete).
• Short-term: add a fallback path that bypasses the lock for bootstrap when we detect stall patterns (in progress, ETA 1 week).
• Mid-term: add a synthetic load test that simulates burst bootstrap patterns and surface regressions in CI (ETA 3 weeks).
• Operational: update runbooks and add a runbook check that the on-call can flip to avoid the autoscale policy during unusual bursts.

If you’d like more detail or a dedicated technical briefing for your team, we’re happy to schedule one. Thank you for your patience.

— Priya on behalf of Redwood Inference Ops

Alice Chen: This is great. Couple of edits: distill the impact numbers (we have exact % and list of orgs impacted), and add the SLA note.

Priya Raman: Updated draft with numbers. New paragraph: Impacted volume was ~3.2% of requests across the affected region, and roughly 12 customers experienced transient errors; our SREs have a list and we can send bespoke notes if needed. The incident did not trigger our 99.9% monthly SLA window for any single customer.

Miguel Torres: For the internal timeline, please include the handoff at 14:30 UTC — I joined the page then for kernel-level tracing. Also add that the incident-bot created the page ID INC-2026-3214.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3214 created at 14:07 UTC. Severity: P2. On-call: Alice Chen. Postmortem status: draft.

Priya Raman: OK adding that. Also, we should prep a short status-page update:
Status page suggested text:
"Between 14:06–14:44 UTC we experienced elevated errors and latency for text-generation endpoints in our us-west-2 region. A fix was deployed at 14:42 UTC and service returned to normal. A post-incident analysis is underway. We will update this page with findings and mitigations."

Samir Patel: +1. Might be good to add a line about no customer data exposure.

Priya Raman: Added.

Marco (support): Do we want to queue up one-off customer notifications for the 12 impacted customers? I can draft personalized notes once I get the list.

Alice Chen: Please do. Miguel — can you share the list (just org names and impacted endpoints)? Keep sensitive details out.

Miguel Torres: Sharing list now in a separate secure doc.

Priya Raman: Next steps I’ll take:
• Finalize the customer email and status page text (this thread).
• Coordinate sending account-specific notes for the 12 impacted orgs (Marco).
• Ensure the postmortem (RCA) gets uploaded to incidents and link included in status page.

Alice Chen: I’m going to add the follow-ups to the runbook duties: verify the patch rollouts and owner for synthetic test. Miguel will own the CI synthetic test. Samir to validate patch in staging.

Samir Patel: Got it. I’ll run a canary validation pass across staging now and post results.

incident-bot: Change log: postmortem updated at 17:20 UTC. Next review scheduled 3 days.

Priya Raman: Thanks team — I’ll post the final customer email in this thread when done. If anyone has edits to the draft please flag before 17:00 UTC.

Alice Chen: One last ask: add a short blameless note in the email: we’ll avoid naming individuals and focus on systems and mitigations.

Priya Raman: Done. Final draft pushed below. Ready to send once Marco confirms recipient list.

Marco (support): I have the list and will start sending personalized notes after legal signs off. ETA 2 hours.

Priya Raman: Perfect, closing the loop here. I’ll link the incidents postmortem once it’s published. Thanks everyone.
